samples.description: Full-sample U.S.-incorporated firm-years with nonmissing one-year Δ/MVA1, nonmissing CTE and current total assets, paper corporation exclusions, and observation years 1988–2014; firms require at least five eligible (not necessarily consecutive) observations. Uses documented best-effort current FIC/STKO approximations and currency-compatible construction.

assumptions: Use FYEAR as observation year for TIME=FYEAR−1988 and the 34% schedule in 1988–1992; the paper prints the descending typo “1998 through 1992.”
Use current ISO FIC=USA as an approximation to legacy FIC/FINC=0; the local field is labeled current, not historical.

Use current COMPANY.STKO and FUNDA.CONM because no dated fields are cataloged; use SEC_IDHIST for dated CUSIP when unique, with a documented current/header fallback. Follow FN14’s explicit STKO=1/2 and STKO=0 missing-price exclusions despite Table 3 wording.
Use SEC_MTHPRC.CURCDM only after same-GVKEY/HIID/date PRCCM agrees with FUNDQ.PRCCQ within one cent; otherwise use the authorized beginning-AT fallback when available.

Keep stable reporting-currency Δ native; convert mismatched beginning price to beginning statement currency at the exact date. Translate only actual mixed reporting histories to USD with EXRAT12M for flows and EXRATD for stocks.
Use pooled 1st/99th percentile winsorization on the common-eligible full-period sample before the five-observation firm filter; SAS PCTLDEF=5 default.
Use ivreg2 small-sample inference for reported t statistics; two-way finite-sample correction is best effort because the paper does not specify it.
Companion descriptive exports for actual estimation rows are tables/table6c_all_desc.{md,rtf,csv,tex}.

limitations: The assignment uses current-header incorporation, ownership, and name classifications for historical rows because exact dated FIC/STKO/name fields are absent from the cataloged local products; dated CUSIP history is used where SEC_IDHIST uniquely supports it.

The paper does not specify FYEAR versus calendar-year(DATADATE), percentile grouping/order, percentile algorithm, or exact two-way finite-sample degrees-of-freedom correction; documented best-effort choices are in design.md.
